Cost of revenues consists primarily of employee salaries, incentives, and benefits for personnel directly involved in delivering software products, operating SaaS infrastructure, and providing support, implementation and consulting services; overhead, facilities and data center costs; software royalty fees; consumer reporting agency data and processing services; third-party hosting fees related to our SaaS services; travel costs; and outside services.

The fiscal 2025 over 2024 increase in cost of revenues of $5.5 million was primarily attributable to an $8.7 million increase in infrastructure and facilities costs, partially offset by a $2.1 million decrease in outside services costs and a $1.4 million decrease in personnel and labor costs. The increase in infrastructure and facilities costs was primarily attributable to an increase in third-party data center hosting costs and an increase in depreciation on data center computer hardware. The decrease in outside services costs was primarily attributable to decreased third-party contractor costs. The decrease in personnel and labor costs was primarily attributable to decreased incentive expense. Cost of revenues as a percentage of revenues decreased to 18 % during fiscal 2025 from 20% during fiscal 2024, primarily due to increased sales of our higher-margin Scores products.

rd.heading: Research and Development
rd.text:
Research and development expenses include personnel and related overhead costs incurred in the development of new products and services, including research of mathematical and statistical models and development of new versions of Software products.

The fiscal 2025 over 2024 increase in research and development expenses of $16.4 million was primarily attributable to a $6.9 million increase in infrastructure and facilities costs, a $5.7 million increase in outside services costs, and a $3.8 million increase in personnel and labor costs. The increase in infrastructure and facilities costs was primarily attributable to increased third-party data center hosting costs and third-party SaaS services costs. The increase in outside services costs was primarily attributable to increased third-party contractor costs. The increase in personnel and labor costs was primarily attributable to increased headcount. Research and development expenses as a percentage of revenues decreased to 9% during fiscal 2025 from 10% during fiscal 2024.

The fiscal 2025 over 2024 increase in net interest expense of $28.0 million was primarily attributable to the $1.5 billion of 2025 Senior Notes (as defined below), partially offset by a lower average outstanding balance and a lower average interest rate on borrowings under our credit agreement during fiscal 2025.

sbc.heading: Share-Based Compensation
sbc.text: We measure share-based compensation cost at the grant date based on the fair value of the award and recognize it as expense, net of estimated forfeitures, over the vesting or service period, as applicable, of the stock award (generally three to four years). We use the Black-Scholes valuation model to determine the fair value of our stock options and a Monte Carlo valuation model to determine the fair value of our market share units. Our valuation models and generally accepted valuation techniques require us to make assumptions and to apply judgment to determine the fair value of our awards. These assumptions and judgments include estimating the volatility of our stock price, expected dividend yield, employee turnover rates and employee stock option exercise behaviors. For the periods presented, we have not experienced significant changes to our estimates and judgments related to the fair value of our awards. See Note 13 to the accompanying consolidated financial statements for further discussion of our share-based employee benefit plans.

lines.name: Long-term debt

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, revenues generated from our agreements with Experian, TransUnion and Equifax collectively accounted for 60%, 51% and 45% of our total revenues, respectively.
Our largest market segment is financial services, representing 92% of our total revenue during fiscal 2026.
Our largest geographic market is the Americas, representing 89% of our total revenue during fiscal 2026.
During fiscal 2026, 92% of our revenues were derived from sales of products and services to the banking industry.

During fiscal 2026, 20% of our revenues was derived from business outside the U.S. As part of our growth strategy, we plan to continue to pursue opportunities outside the U.S., including opportunities in countries with economic systems that are in early stages of development and that may not mature sufficiently to result in growth for our business.

Revenues collectively generated by agreements with these customers accounted for 60 %, 51 % and 45 % of our total revenues in fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively, with all three consumer reporting agencies each contributing more than 10 % of our total revenues in each of fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024.
At September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, three customers and two customers, respectively, accounted for 10 % or more of total consolidated receivables.
We rely on a combination of patent, copyright, trademark and trade secret laws and confidentiality agreements and procedures to protect our proprietary rights.

The applicable requirements depend upon the monetary value of the awarded contract, the particular government agency awarding or funding the contract, the scope of services to be delivered, and the level of access that the agency will need to provide to us to enable us to perform the contract.

Our revenue growth and the success of our business strategy depend on our ability to enhance and improve existing products and services, including FICO ® Platform, and to continue to introduce new products and services that keep pace with technological developments, satisfy increasingly sophisticated customer requirements, and achieve market acceptance.
Our revenue growth and strategy success also depend on our ability to adopt new software engineering technologies and processes, including AI-based software design and development platforms.
We also believe that much of the future growth of our business and the success of our business strategy depends on our ability to continue to expand into newer markets for our products and services.
We rely on relatively few customers, including our contracts with the three major consumer reporting agencies, for a significant portion of our revenues and profits.
We rely on relationships with third parties for technologies used in our products, and for marketing, distribution, deployment, and certain other services.
Our business relies on third-party technologies and service providers throughout the product lifecycle, from development to deployment to customers.
In addition, we rely on distributors, resellers, or partners to market and distribute our products and we expect to continue expanding these relationships.
We rely upon proprietary technology rights, and if we are unable to protect them, our business could be harmed.

Our ability to provide reliable products and services to our customers depends on the efficient and uninterrupted operation of our data centers, information technology, and communication systems, as well as those of our external service providers.
